questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of Open-Weight LLMs?
options: A. They are always higher performing frontier models.
B. They have variable costs and credit allowances.
C. They are reproducible and private if run locally.
D. They are easier to use/deploy via interfaces.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as an example of a Closed-Weight LLM?
According to the footnote on Slide 4, what do open and closed APIs allow you to do?
options: B. Send requests to an LLM service and receive model responses programmatically.
C. Run models locally without internet access.
D. Access the training data directly.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'knowledge cutoff date' in LLMs?
options: A. To determine the cost of the model.
B. To clarify how up-to-date their training data is.
C. To limit the number of parameters.

questions.question: Which of the following is cited as an example of a fully open model in the context of training data?
According to the slide on Model Size and 'Intelligence', what tradeoffs should be considered when choosing a model?
options: B. Size vs. knowledge vs. performance vs. cost

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a benchmark evaluation tool?
In the 'Cost per Task' chart on the Benchmark Evaluation slide, what does a lower value indicate?
options: B. Lower weighted average cost (USD) per Intelligence Index task.
